slot.brief: Point given in 3D; find its perpendicular distance from a coordinate axis (say the y-axis) using the formula √(x² + z²).

stem: The perpendicular distance of the point $(3,-4,12)$ from the $y$-axis is

verdicts.working: The distance from the y-axis is \(\sqrt{x^2+z^2}=\sqrt{3^2+12^2}=3\sqrt{17}\).

working:
$d=\sqrt{x^2+z^2}=\sqrt{3^2+12^2}=\sqrt{153}=3\sqrt{17}$

Independent check: The distance from the y-axis is \(\sqrt{x^2+z^2}=\sqrt{3^2+12^2}=3\sqrt{17}\).
solution:
The perpendicular distance of $(x,y,z)$ from the $y$-axis is $d=\sqrt{x^2+z^2}$.
$$d=\sqrt{3^2+12^2}=\sqrt{153}=3\sqrt{17}$$
